title: Keeping the Ball Rolling: Fullerene-like Molecular Clusters
claim: Ligands can contribute to a fullerene-like core in two distinct ways: their atoms may form part of its polyhedral skeleton, or they may bridge a skeleton whose vertices are metal atoms only.
explanation: The review contrasts the P/Cu framework assembled from pentaphosphaferrocene and copper halides with lanthanide–nickel clusters whose metal-only polyhedra are supported by bridging ligands.
caveats: The distinction describes core topology, not the absence of ligands from a metal-only-vertex cluster.
